recorded_from_commit: card/200-page-numbers-and-toc (implementation commit, after CARD-201/CARD-202 merged into main)
recorded_from_commit_note: Recorded against this card's own implementation: a table of contents page is inserted between the guide and the puzzle section, and every interior page gains a bottom-outer-corner folio. Pages 1-2 (the guide) carry only the new folio; page 3 is new (the TOC); every page from 4 onward is CARD-201/CARD-202's own content, shifted by exactly one page (this book's TOC is one page) and carrying the new folio too.
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages — the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-200 adds a table-of-contents page after the guide and a page-number folio on every interior page but the cover. Both are new ink: the TOC is an entirely new page (3), and the folio adds a small mark to the bottom-outer corner of every other page, so every one of this book's thirteen pages carries different pixels from CARD-201's own twelve-page recording, even where the content above the footer band (the grid, the clues, the band, the answer caption) is byte-for-byte what it always was. See tests/test_book_pdf_memory.py's TestBookPdfMemory_ContentAboveTheFooterBandIsUnchanged for the test that verifies that narrower claim directly, by content rather than by a whole-page digest (the same 'compare by content, not by raw bytes' technique CARD-201's own TestBookPdfMemory_EveryPageAfterTheGuideIsByteIdenticalShiftedByOne uses for its own parity-shift) — this fixture is the forward baseline for the next card, not itself the proof that nothing but the footer moved.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like with CARD-200's page numbers and table of contents in place. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, and an interior_bytes/colour_interior_bytes that no longer matches means the written file changed. If a later card deliberately changes either, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
interior_colorspace_note: What every page of this interior declares (CARD-147's own fact, unaffected by CARD-201). NOT the same as each page entry's 'mode' below, which is 'RGB' and always will be: that field is what tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages normalises every page to before digesting it, regardless of the file's own declared colour space.
font_fingerprint_note: This machine's Arial-or-fallback fingerprint, reproduced before this file was written (tests.helpers.book_corpus.font_fingerprint). A machine with a different fingerprint skips the font_dependent_pages below rather than failing on them.
font_dependent_pages_note: Both guide pages (1, 2), the new TOC page (3, CARD-200: its title and every entry are set through _guide_face, the same Arial-or-fallback path the guide and divider pages already use), the three level dividers (4, 6, 8) and the SOLUTIONS divider (10) are machine-lettered. None of the three packed/full answer pages (11-13) are machine-lettered -- a packed slot's band and caption letter in the packaged DejaVu Sans, and so does every page's own new folio (CARD-200: it reuses _band_font, the same packaged face, exactly as the answer caption does -- G-4's reuse, not a new font path), so the folio never makes an otherwise machine-safe page machine-dependent.
interior_bytes_note: The black-and-white interior of this book: 3420073 bytes, where CARD-201's own recording (no TOC, no folio) held 3310666. The difference is the new TOC page's own JPEG stream plus every page's new folio mark.
colour_interior_bytes_note: The same book with a COLOUR interior: 3775345 bytes, where the stale recording held 3985305. Read by tests/test_book_pdf_ink_mode.py only to show the length is longer than the black-and-white file's, never compared byte-for-byte against any earlier recording.
changed_pages_note: Every page's digest moved: pages 1-2 gained the new folio mark alone, page 3 is entirely new (the TOC), and every page from 4 onward both shifted position (this book's one TOC page) and gained the new folio mark. 'Changed' here is therefore the whole book, not a subset -- the narrower 'nothing but the footer band moved' claim is verified separately, by content, in TestBookPdfMemory_ContentAboveTheFooterBandIsUnchanged.
